## House effects

The average difference between each pollster's published numbers and the model's estimate of true support, in
percentage points, at current support levels. Positive means the pollster tends to report a higher number.

```{python}
if site.house is not None:
    site.show("house")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if site.house is None:
    print("No pollster has published enough polls this term to estimate its house effect.")
```

## How well has the model done in the past? {#track-record}

```{python}
#| include: false
design = site.design_facts()
```

Each model was refitted using only the polls published `{python} design["horizons"]` weeks before the
`{python} design["targets"]` elections, and scored against the result. CRPS is the average error of the whole
forecast distribution in percentage points; lower is better. The 90% coverage should be close to 0.9.
[How the model is tested](evaluation.qmd).

## About the model

Weekly support for `{python} len(site.parties) - 1` parties and "Other" follows a correlated random walk, pinned
to the official results of the `{python} site.cfg.anchor_election`–`{python} site.last_result_year` elections.
Each poll is read through its pollster's house effect and an industry-wide polling error. The
{{< var election.year >}} election-day error cannot be seen yet, so it is drawn from past elections, with
heavy tails and a wider spread for parties that are small or have never been elected. Variants are
combined with weights from backtests, and seats follow the MMP rules. [How the model works](model.qmd).

```{python}
#| output: asis

```
